newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's Hariri heads for Clinton meeting.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's Hariri heads for Clinton meeting.

text.p: Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri flew to Paris on Tuesday en route for a meeting with U.S. President Bill Clinton on Friday.
Lebanese officials said Hariri would meet Clinton at the White House to discuss financing Lebanon's reconstruction programme, stalled Middle East peace talks and regional developments.

Hariri left Beirut for a private visit to Paris immediately after he and his government resigned in the wake of recent parliamentary elections to allow the formation of a new cabinet which he is also expected to head.
Hariri, in office since October 1992, is staying on in a caretaker capacity until the formation of the new government which is expected around the end of October.

Officials said the Hariri-Clinton talks would include plans for a meeting of a consultative group of nations being formed by the United States -- including France, the European Union, Russia and other countries -- to help finance Lebanon's reconstruction.
Acting Finance Minister Fouad Siniora, who accompanied Hariri, has said Lebanon will ask the group for $5 billion over five years in soft loans and donations.
The group was set up in April under a U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon which killed 200 people and caused $500 million damage.

Hariri requested the meeting with Clinton after an expected meeting of the group scheduled for Friday was postponed. U.S. Ambassador in Beirut Richard Jones has said it will hold its first meeting after the November 5 U.S. presidential election.
